rfm_tuples.R: As of December 31, 2024, the Company owned 221 hotels with an aggregate of 29,764 guest rooms located in urban, high-end suburban and developing markets throughout 37 states and the District of Columbia, including two hotels with a total of 206 guest rooms classified as held for sale (10-K).
rfm_tuples.f: Cross-check property count vs Q1 2025 10-Q (filed 2025-05-01, pre-cutoff). Verify dispositions match.
rfm_tuples.M_value: Q1 2025 10-Q reports 219 hotels with 29,558 rooms as of 3/31/2025, including 1 hotel held for sale. Reconciles cleanly: 221 (12/31) minus 2 sold in Q1 (Feb 2025, March 2025 for combined $21M) = 219. No claim drift on property count.
rfm_tuples.interpretation: Hotel inventory disclosure is internally consistent across 10-K and Q1 10-Q; sales executed at gain (~$3.6M Q1 gain on $21M proceeds).

rfm_tuples.R: The Company expects low single digit RevPAR growth for its Comparable Hotels for 2025 as compared to 2024, which is comparable to broader industry expectations (10-K, Feb 24, 2025).
rfm_tuples.f: Compare to Q1 2025 10-Q outlook (filed May 1, 2025, ~10 weeks later).
rfm_tuples.M_value: Q1 10-Q outlook downgraded: 'The Company expects RevPAR for its Comparable Hotels to seasonally improve and RevPAR for the full year of 2025 to be in line with 2024' — flat, not 'low single digit growth'. Q1 Same Store RevPAR was -0.1% YoY; Comparable Hotels RevPAR -0.5%; Adjusted Hotel EBITDA -4.1%. Company cited weather, reduced government travel in late March, macroeconomic uncertainty. Government demand softened 'due to recent changes made by the current administration to curtail government spending'.
rfm_tuples.interpretation: Real claim drift within 10 weeks of 10-K issuance: growth guide cut to flat. Disclosure is honest (named the federal-spending headwind) but signals the 10-K's optimism was already stale.

rfm_tuples.R: The Company has historically maintained and plans in the future to maintain relatively low leverage... The Company's ratio of total debt, net of cash, to total capitalization... as of December 31, 2024 was 28.5%. (10-K)
rfm_tuples.f: Cross-check debt schedule and revolver capacity; verify $295M 2025 maturity is coverable.
rfm_tuples.M_value: Total debt $1.48B; 2025 maturities $295M ($225M variable + $70M fixed). Revolving Credit Facility unused capacity $567.5M at 12/31/2024 and $500.2M at 3/31/2025 — covers 2025 wall ~2x. Weighted avg interest rate 4.71%. $130M term loan extended in July 2024 from $85M, maturity pushed to July 2026. No going-concern language; no covenant violations disclosed.
rfm_tuples.interpretation: Leverage modest for hotel REITs (28.5% LTV-equivalent), maturity wall is well within revolver capacity, recent amendment shows lender support not coercion.

rfm_tuples.R: Auditor change disclosure: KPMG appointed effective 2/22/2024; E&Y dismissed after FY2023 audit. 'There were no disagreements... and no reportable events.' (8-K 2024-02-23, Item 4.01)
rfm_tuples.f: Run auditor_change_tracker; scan filing text for resignation/disagreement language.
rfm_tuples.M_value: Both detectors flag UPGRADE_OR_LATERAL (Big-4 to Big-4). 8-K text confirms competitive RFP selection, no disagreements, no reportable events. KPMG's FY2024 audit (Feb 24, 2025) issued clean unqualified opinion plus clean ICFR attestation. E&Y also issued clean prior-year report.
rfm_tuples.interpretation: Auditor change is well-documented routine rotation after E&Y's 16-year tenure (2007-2023), not a forensic red flag. Mode-B check: would expect resignation language or scope/disagreement notes if hostile — none present.

rfm_tuples.R: 'There are no material concentrations of 10% or more of total revenues allocated to a single customer for the reporting periods presented.' Each hotel treated as separate operating segment. Marriott + Hilton brands dominate; 16 unaffiliated mgmt companies. (10-K, Note on Segments)
rfm_tuples.f: Verify concentration claim by brand and geography distributions.
rfm_tuples.M_value: Brand concentration: largest brand Hilton Garden Inn = 39 hotels / 221 = 17.6% of hotels. Top 4 brands (HGI, Hampton, Courtyard, Residence Inn) = 138/221 = 62.4%. Geographic: California 26, Texas 26 (each ~11.8% of hotels). All under Marriott or Hilton umbrellas (substantially all). Customer-level concentration claim is technically correct (no single hotel customer); brand-platform concentration on Marriott+Hilton is real but disclosed.
rfm_tuples.interpretation: Concentration disclosure is accurate as worded. Mode-B observation: dependence on Marriott + Hilton franchise standards is a structural risk but transparently flagged ('Substantially all of the Company's hotels operate under Marriott or Hilton brands').

rfm_tuples.R: 'While management currently expects monthly cash distributions to continue at $0.08 per common share...' Annual rate $0.96/share. $243.7M total distributions paid in 2024, incl. $31.2M special distribution declared Dec 2024. (10-K + Q1 10-Q)
rfm_tuples.f: Check distribution coverage via MFFO and operating cash flow.
rfm_tuples.M_value: MFFO FY2024 = $388.5M (vs $366.9M FY2023, $351.4M FY2022) — three straight years of growth. Distributions of $243.7M = ~62.7% MFFO payout (including $31.2M special). Q1 2025 distributions $69.6M vs cash from ops; revolver tapped +$92.5M / paid $27M (seasonal, disclosed practice). Special distribution declared in DEC 2024 (NOT a cut) indicates strong 2024 cash flow.
rfm_tuples.interpretation: Distribution is well-covered by MFFO with substantial cushion; a special distribution declared 2 months before 10-K is the opposite of a distress signal.

rfm_tuples.R: Mode-B derivation: Given the 10-K's confident 'low single digit RevPAR growth' guide and clean ICFR, would expect zero insider selling and possibly some clustered buying if mgmt believes shares are undervalued post-cutoff drawdown (-23.7%).
rfm_tuples.f: Pull Form 4 filings 2024-08-01 through 2025-05-15; classify codes (P/S/A/F/G).
rfm_tuples.M_value: Zero S-code (open-market sale) transactions in entire H2 2024 and through 2025-05-15. Insider activity restricted to F (tax withholding on vesting), A (equity grants), G (gifts). EXPLICIT CLUSTER OF OPEN-MARKET PURCHASES May 6-9, 2025 (immediately after Q1 10-Q filing): Exec Chairman Glade M. Knight $114,300 (10,000 sh @ $11.43); CFO Perkins $24,612 (2,100 sh @ $11.72); CAO Labrecque $11,450 (1,000 sh @ $11.45); Director Hugh Redd $11,370; Director Woolley $22,690. Director Handlon also bought $99,289 on March 12, 2025. Total cluster-buy ~$285K from 6 insiders within ~9 weeks of cutoff.
rfm_tuples.interpretation: Strongest single bullish signal in this dossier. Cross-functional cluster buying (Chairman, CFO, CAO, 2+ Directors) at depressed prices, right after the guidance cut, is highly inconsistent with mgmt secretly knowing of impairment. Mode-B verification of the optimistic forward-looking statements gets a strong positive.

rfm_tuples.R: Mode-B derivation: Glade M. Knight (Executive Chairman) was founder of multiple prior Apple REIT entities and runs Apple Realty Group ('ARG') + Energy 11 / Energy Resources 12. Related-party disclosures must be material-light and transparent.
rfm_tuples.f: Verify related-party transactions disclosed are limited and reimbursed at cost; check for Apple-REIT-family entanglements not disclosed.
rfm_tuples.M_value: Total related-party reimbursements: $1.5M 2024 / $1.2M 2023 / $1.0M 2022 — small (<0.2% of revenue). Cost-sharing structure for support services to ARG (which serves Energy 11 / Energy Resources 12). Trailing receivables ~$0.5M each year-end, settled quarterly. Mr. Knight's conflicts-of-interest are disclosed under Risk Factors. EDGAR FTS for 'Apple Hospitality lawsuit' returned 402 hits but no direct litigation flags against APLE (most hits are unrelated boilerplate from other filers).
rfm_tuples.interpretation: Related-party amounts are small and transparently disclosed. Historical Apple-REIT-family litigation (Apple REIT Six/Seven/Eight/Nine FINRA-era issues from ~2011-2013) pre-date current company; no fresh disclosure issues.

rfm_tuples.R: Mode-B derivation: Pre-cutoff drawdown -23.7% with no going-concern, no covenant breach, no auditor resignation, distribution intact, special distribution declared — what is the explainer?
rfm_tuples.f: Cross-reference 10-K + Q1 10-Q for unfavorable macro/sector context.
rfm_tuples.M_value: Disclosed headwinds: (a) RevPAR growth slowed to 2.5% in 2024 from prior years; (b) Q1 2025 turned slightly negative; (c) federal government travel cutbacks under 'current administration'; (d) interest expense up ($19.4M vs $17.3M YoY Q1) from variable-rate debt + higher SOFR; (e) hotel sector cyclical sensitivity. Q1 Adjusted Hotel EBITDA -4.1%. No undisclosed problems found in filings.
rfm_tuples.interpretation: The drawdown looks earned from real-but-disclosed macro/sector softening (rate environment + federal-travel cut), not concealment. The forward 'low single digit RevPAR growth' claim in the 10-K had to be walked back to 'flat' 10 weeks later, which is a soft underdelivery on a stated expectation.

rfm_tuples.R: 'Substantially all of the Company's hotels operate under Marriott or Hilton brands...' Brand table totals 221 hotels.

rfm_tuples.M_value: Brand table sum: HGI 39 + Hampton 36 + Courtyard 34 + Residence Inn 30 + Homewood 29 + Fairfield 10 + Home2 10 + SpringHill 9 + TownePlace 8 + Embassy 4 + AC 4 + Hyatt Place 3 + Marriott 2 + Hyatt House 2 + Aloft 1 = 221 (matches). summary: Apple Hospitality REIT is a transparent boring-middle name with no forensic-disclosure red flags as of 2025-05-15. The -23.7% drawdown is explained by real-but-disclosed cyclical softening: 2024 RevPAR growth moderated to 2.5%, Q1 2025 turned slightly negative (Same Store -0.1%), and management explicitly cited reduced federal-government travel from administration spending cuts. The only honest claim drift is a guidance walk-down from 'low single digit RevPAR growth' (10-K Feb 24) to 'in line with 2024' (Q1 10-Q May 1) — a moderate underdelivery on a forward statement, not a concealment. Counter-evidence is strong: clean Big-4 auditor change with no disagreements, no going-concern language, MFFO grew 3 years running, $31.2M special distribution declared in Dec 2024, $500M+ revolver cushion vs $295M 2025 maturities, and a striking cluster of insider OPEN-MARKET PURCHASES May 6-9 by Executive Chairman ($114K), CFO, CAO, and two directors right after Q1 results. Zero insider selling all year. Verdict LONG-tier.
